amendments.what: Both OPEN questions closed with dev's implementation answers, folded into the scenarios they govern (S06 setup + mechanism, S10 failure surface). NO EXPECTATION CHANGED — the amendment records mechanisms, which were dev's to declare, not bars, which were mine to set. The open list is emptied rather than deleted so the amendment shows what it closed.

THE NINE RETAINED v2 SCENARIOS GAIN THEIR EXPECTATIONS. They were nine bare NAMES — a bar with no value in it, which is my omission and not dev's; dev found it, refused to guess, and raised it. They ARE scored: pass criterion (1) says 'every scenario' and the v2 text they are retained from required an exact expected event sequence for each. Expectations derived from v2's own words (kind, reason, seq order — the digest-transitions clause is dead by v3 F5) resolved against §4a's per-write kind rule and §4b's site table. FOUR of the nine expand into CELLS rather than one expectation, because the spec names more than one path and picking would be my choice: confirm (byte-delta present/absent), absorb (survivor restated/created), expiry (lapsed/decayed), import (created/mutated/no-event). Two are asserted as sets within a batch rather than ordered sequences, because the spec demotes intra-batch order to 'the append order the database serialized' and pins the BATCH as the atomic unit. Criterion (5) added so a runner cannot satisfy the gate while skipping them.

V05 (absorb) CORRECTED — amendment 2 had it wrong, and the error was mine reading the spec, not a gap in the spec. §4b's `mutated` row says 'absorption restate' and its `created` row says 'insert_incoming, absorption survivor'; those name two DIFFERENT EDGES, and I read them as two fates of one. The restate is the ABSORBED PRIOR (note extended with `absorbed_by:<survivor>`), the survivor IS the incoming and is new by construction (graph.py:426, 'The survivor IS the incoming (a NEW row)'). So there is ONE shape, not two cells: three events in one txn — absorbed mutated, absorbed invalidated/absorbed_duplicate, survivor created. Amendment 2's cell (a) named a path that does not exist and its cell (b) omitted the absorbed edge's restate. The correction REDUCES the bar: an 'exhaust the class' instinct manufactured a second cell for a path there was no evidence for, which is the same over-broad error in a bar that it would be in a claim. Ordering within the batch is still not asserted; instead the PAYLOADS are pinned (§4a's post-mutation-state rule), which constrains the sequence using what the spec does determine. Also records dev's V08 import mechanism, which closes the short-circuit confound research flagged.

retained_v2_scenarios.REQUIRED_ONE_BATCH: all three carry the SAME txn — an absorption is one atomic mutation and a cutoff includes or excludes it whole
retained_v2_scenarios.REQUIRED_PAYLOADS: asserted on CONTENT rather than on seq order, which the spec does not set: §4a's payload rule makes each event's `state` the edge's full serialization AFTER that mutation, so the absorbed edge's `mutated` state carries the EXTENDED note (`absorbed_by:<survivor>`) and its `invalidated` state carries that note AND the invalidation fields. Pinning the payloads constrains the sequence without asserting an order the spec leaves to 'the append order the database serialized' — a stronger assertion made from what the spec does determine.
retained_v2_scenarios.name: absorb — ONE shape, not two
retained_v2_scenarios.spec_cite: specs/0029 §4b table: `mutated` <- `_upsert_edge_row` (note-append, ABSORPTION RESTATE, counter-bearing re-upserts); `created` <- `apply_supersession_plan` (INSERT_INCOMING, ABSORPTION SURVIVOR). The two phrases name DIFFERENT EDGES and the row already says which: the restate is the ABSORBED PRIOR (re-upserted with its note extended by `absorbed_by:<survivor>`), and the survivor IS the insert_incoming. `absorbed_duplicate` is a registered retaining reason (specs/0004 W8/W-Q1). §4a: one event-emitting write transaction = ONE txn.
retained_v2_scenarios.why_one_shape: There is NO survivor-restate path: the survivor is the incoming edge and is new by construction. Amendment 2's two cells were my misreading of the §4b row — I read 'absorption restate' and 'absorption survivor' as two fates of ONE edge when the row names two DIFFERENT edges. Splitting into cells here would invent a path rather than exhaust a class.

scenarios.failure_surface_declared_by_dev_2026_09_: The DEFERRED schedule is executed by the seam model's runner (specs/evidence/0029-0030/seam_model/allocation_schedule.py::run_two_connection_schedule(path, deferred_batch, busy_timeout_ms=0)), NEVER by the product store — the product path only knows BEGIN IMMEDIATE. With busy_timeout 0 the loser raises sqlite3.OperationalError carrying sqlite's verbatim 'database is locked', immediately. In the PRODUCT store the analogous refusal (_write_txn cannot take the write lock after the 0007 busy wait) re-raises sqlite3.OperationalError whose message EMBEDS the original text, so the assertion is on the SUBSTRING 'locked' and holds on both paths. 'No partial batch persists' is checked twice: the runner's seqs-disjointness assertion and the corpus runner's whole-batch check.
